newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam president sparks conflicting health reports.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam president sparks conflicting health reports.

text.p: Vietnamese government sources said on Friday that President Le Duc Anh was recovering a week after he was taken to hospital with blood pressure problems, but there were other conflicting reports on his health.
The sources said the 75-year-old general, who belongs to the communist country's ageing leadership troika, had recovered well enough to walk around at the Hanoi 108 Army Hospital.
"He's getting better," said one, who declined to give further details.

But other sources, including diplomats, said earlier in the week that Anh had been paralysed down one side of his body by a stroke and quoted doctors as saying it was unlikely he would recover sufficiently to resume his duties.
The official media, explaining Anh's absence from a welcoming ceremony for visiting South Korean President Kim Young-sam, ackowledged for the first time on Thursday Anh was ill.
But government officials have since said they can give no update on his condition.
While Anh is incapacitated, Vice President Nguyen Thi Binh will act in his place. If he was to be replaced, the choice of successor would have to be approved by the National Assembly.

Analysts say replacing him would be difficult as he occupies a key position of influence over the military and security apparatus. His departure could reopen an internal debate over succession which had simmered ahead of a key party congress in June.
Other top leaders are the reformist Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet, 73, and Communist Party Secretary General Do Muoi, 79.
All three had been expected to resign at the congress, but the party opted instead for an extension of their terms in office.
